question.problem:
Find the shortest distance between the origin and the osculating plane for the curve $r(t)$ at the point where $t=\pi ,$ given that

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨-3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,4t,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ T(t) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,4,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ N(t) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $T$ and $N$ denote the unit tangent and principal normal, respectively.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that the unit tangent and the principal normal at the point where $t=\pi $ are

$$
\begin{aligned}T(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{5}⟨3\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,4,\,3\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩=\frac{1}{5}⟨0,4,-3⟩ \\ N(\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩=⟨-1,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, the position vector of the point where $t=\pi $ is

$$
p=r(\pi )=⟨-3\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,4\pi ,\,3\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩=⟨3,4\pi ,0⟩.
$$

Now, we need to find a vector that's perpendicular to the osculating plane. To do that, we use the cross product of the unit tangent $T(\pi )$ and the principal normal $N(\pi ):$

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =T(\pi )\times N(\pi ) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,4,-3⟩\times ⟨-1,0,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 4 & -3 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\frac{1}{5}[\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k\text{ }] \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(3\,j+4\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}⟨0,3,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the shortest distance between our plane and the origin is given by

$$
d=\frac{|(p-0)\cdot n|}{‖n‖}=\frac{|p\cdot n|}{‖n‖}=|p\cdot n|,
$$

since $‖n‖=1.$ Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =|p\cdot n| \\  & =|⟨3,4\pi ,0⟩\cdot \frac{1}{5}⟨0,3,4⟩| \\  & =\frac{1}{5}|0+12\pi +0| \\  & =\frac{12\pi }{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
